item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01230","case1_error":"Evaluates 80 − 16 as 40 instead of 64.","case2_error":"Evaluates 13 + 7 + 30 as 40 instead of 50 within a correctly formed equation.","reason":"Both incorrectly evaluate numerical expressions despite correctly representing the problem's relationships.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J01231","case1_error":"Evaluates 30 + 35 + 46 as 101 instead of 111.","case2_error":"Uses George's 45 oranges instead of Amelia's 15 apples as the base for George's apple count.","reason":"Case 1 is an arithmetic evaluation error; case 2 establishes an erroneous relation using the wrong quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01232","case1_error":"Counts only one sandwich instead of two and evaluates the listed $32.25 sum as $30.25.","case2_error":"Assigns Felix his brother's lifting capacity using three times the brother's weight.","reason":"Case 1 omits a purchased unit and misadds costs; case 2 substitutes the brother's lifting relation for Felix's.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01233","case1_error":"Applies only two halvings over 30 years, incorrectly assigning the first halving to age 20.","case2_error":"Omits the original ring's $10,000 purchase cost from net spending.","reason":"Case 1 miscounts repeated changes across time intervals; case 2 leaves an expense out of a net-cost calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01234","case1_error":"Correctly derives $12 per chair but gives conflicting leading and concluding answers of $20.","case2_error":"Divides Billy's correctly calculated $8 contribution by two, introducing an unwarranted equal split.","reason":"Case 1 has an answer conflict without a demonstrated calculation error; case 2 adds an unjustified division.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
